record.title: OpenAI publishes an AI-generated proposed Navier-Stokes Millennium resolution with a zero-sorry Lean formalization
record.summary: OpenAI published an analytical proof and Lean 4 formalization claiming breakdown alternatives C and D of the Clay Navier-Stokes Millennium problem: for every positive viscosity, suitable smooth forcing and smooth initial data lead to failure of the required global smooth solution conditions on R^3 and the periodic torus. The public formalization reports zero sorrys for the main results and only standard Lean axioms. Its Comparator target was adapted from Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures commit 8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee dated July 27, 2026, before OpenAI's September search, strengthening statement-fidelity evidence. OpenAI attributes discovery to a large multi-agent internal-model campaign and formal verification to GPT-6 Astra. The event and formal artifact are verified; the mathematical resolution remains an extraordinary primary claim pending independent build, semantic audit, specialist review and formal Clay acceptance.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLIC_ARTIFACT
claims.text: OpenAI publicly released an analytical Navier-Stokes proof and a Lean formalization on September 8, 2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_ARTIFACT_METADATA
claims.text: The public formalization metadata reports zero sorrys for the main Navier-Stokes C/D declarations and only standard permitted Lean axioms.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PROVENANCE
claims.text: OpenAI's Comparator challenge is adapted from Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures commit 8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee dated July 27, 2026, before OpenAI says its Millennium search began on September 1.

claims.label: PRIMARY_EXTRAORDINARY_CLAIM_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW
claims.text: The proof establishes Clay alternatives C and D and resolves the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem.

claims.label: FIRST_PARTY_PROCESS_CLAIM
claims.text: OpenAI says the successful group involved on the order of 10,000 concurrent agents, while the Navier-Stokes effort used 2.7 million messages and about 130 billion output tokens, reaching the resolution after about 88 hours and spending another 17 hours on Lean formalization/verification.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_SCOPE_LIMITATION
claims.text: The result is not evidence for unforced Navier-Stokes blowup: the claimed C/D construction uses a smooth external force, while OpenAI's separate Euler result is unforced.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The public repository labels its review status self-assessed, so release plus formalization should not be conflated with independent mathematical acceptance.

contradictory_evidence: Independent reporting records a public credit/data-provenance dispute involving Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpoge. OpenAI states that neither its researchers nor agents saw their work before public release and denies accessing specific user data; the competing allegations were not adjudicated in this run.
Clay's public materials had not yet been updated to reflect formal acceptance of a new resolution when checked, which is an absence of acceptance rather than evidence that the proof is wrong.

evidence_gaps.description: the research desk has not independently executed the Lean build and Comparator challenge.
A passing formal proof still requires audit that the encoded C/D statements and definitions faithfully match the Clay formulation without exploitable definitional gaps.
No independent specialist consensus or Clay acceptance was established in this pass.
The result does not isolate the contribution of model strength, 10k-agent parallelism, 130B output tokens, human resource steering, Euler cross-pollination or formal verification.
Concurrent-work allegations and OpenAI's denial are unresolved.

brief.importance_rationale: Paradigm-level if the central mathematical claim survives independent review: an AI-driven system producing a valid resolution of a Millennium Prize problem would force a major reassessment of the frontier of automated mathematical and scientific research. It is not 10 because this is one extraordinary result produced with very large bespoke inference and orchestration, independent acceptance is still pending, and transfer to broader scientific discovery or economical autonomous research is not established.
limitations: the research desk has not run lake build or Comparator in an independent environment during this connector-only activation.

A machine-checked theorem can still target an incorrectly or incompletely encoded mathematical statement; the pre-existing comparator materially reduces this risk but does not eliminate the need for semantic audit.
The formalization repository labels review as self-assessed, and no formal Clay acceptance was found in this pass.
OpenAI's process is an extreme-scale system result, not a controlled estimate of the internal model's standalone research capability.
No matched cost or success-rate comparison is available against humans, smaller agent teams, Astra alone, or alternative frontier models on the same problem.
The separate dispute concerning Buckmaster and Alpoge's concurrent work is unresolved and should not be used either to invalidate the proof or to dismiss provenance concerns without evidence.

The public formalization reports zero sorrys for the main results and only standard Lean axioms. Its Comparator target was adapted from Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures commit 8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee dated July 27, 2026, before OpenAI's September search, strengthening statement-fidelity evidence. OpenAI attributes discovery to a large multi-agent internal-model campaign and formal verification to GPT-6 Astra. technical.claimed_result: OpenAI claims the construction establishes Clay statements C and D and therefore resolves the Navier-Stokes existence-and-smoothness Millennium Prize problem. OpenAI also claims the successful Navier-Stokes group involved on the order of 10,000 concurrent agents and that the Navier-Stokes effort used 2.7 million agent messages and about 130 billion output tokens, with discovery after about 88 hours and an additional 17 hours for Lean formalization and verification.
technical.compute_or_cost: OpenAI reports about 2.7 million messages and approximately 130 billion output tokens for the Navier-Stokes effort, with a successful group on the order of 10,000 concurrent agents. It does not disclose a reproducible dollar/GPU-hour breakdown in the primary post. The scale means this should not be read as an ordinary single-agent benchmark datapoint.
technical.demonstrated_result: OpenAI has publicly released a detailed proof artifact and a Lean repository. The repository's formalization metadata reports zero sorrys for the two main Navier-Stokes declarations, with permitted axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The Comparator challenge points to a Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures Navier-Stokes statement at commit 8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee from 2026-07-27; that upstream commit message explicitly says the four open Millennium statements were unchanged. the research desk has verified these repository facts, not the theorem's independent mathematical correctness.
technical.implementation_status: Public proof and Lean source released September 8, 2026. OpenAI says proof discovery completed September 5 and Lean formalization/verification September 6. Independent mathematical acceptance and Clay adjudication are pending.
technical.mechanism: OpenAI says it launched many coordinated agent groups on multiple formulations, shifted resources after a related unforced Euler breakthrough, fed the Euler result into the Navier-Stokes effort, cross-pollinated promising insights using Codex, and updated agents as a stronger internal model became available. The resulting analytic proof constructs a smooth forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes evolution whose velocity becomes singular in finite time while satisfying the smooth-forcing and finite-energy conditions required by Clay alternatives C/D. A separate Lean formalization proves the comparator theorem declarations.
technical.novelty: The combination of a claimed Millennium-problem resolution generated by a frontier multi-agent research system, a public analytical proof, and a machine-checkable formalization against a statement adapted from an independently authored pre-existing formal conjecture is materially stronger evidence than a vendor-only claim or informal benchmark score.
technical.regime: Frontier automated mathematics under extreme parallel agent inference, code/tool access, cached web access, cross-agent information sharing, human-directed resource allocation and formal theorem proving.
technical.reproducibility: The Lean project and Comparator instructions are public and in principle independently buildable. the research desk's current connector runtime cannot execute lake build/Comparator, so reproducibility has not yet been independently exercised in this run. Mathematical semantic fidelity and proof acceptance remain open even if the Lean build passes.
technical.strongest_baseline: The strongest present control is the pre-existing Formal Conjectures comparator statement, which predates the OpenAI search and reduces post-hoc statement weakening. The missing stronger controls are an independent clean build/Comparator run, expert audit of formal definitions against the Clay text, independent analytic proof review, and comparison against similarly resourced human or alternative-agent research campaigns.

brief.title: OpenAI publishes an AI-generated proposed Navier-Stokes Millennium resolution with a zero-sorry Lean formalization
brief.why_it_matters: If the proof survives independent scrutiny, this is both a major mathematical result and unusually strong evidence that frontier AI systems can generate new research at the level of a Millennium Prize problem when given extreme parallel inference, tool access and formal verification. It would materially change automated-science planning, but the result cannot yet be interpreted as a clean measure of a single model's autonomous capability because OpenAI reports roughly 10,000 concurrent agents, enormous token use, resource steering, cross-group consolidation and a separate formalization phase.
